title: On the Gravitational-Wave Energy Density in the Teleparallel Equivalent of General Relativity: Application to LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA Events
content: We compute the gravitational energy density of a linearized gravitational wave in the teleparallel equivalent of general relativity. For a plane wave in the transverse-traceless gauge we obtain the closed and exact expression \( \varepsilon(u)=\tfrac{1}{32\pi}\,\tfrac{d^{2}}{du^{2}}(h_{+}^{2}+h_{\times}^{2}) \), and evaluate it on model polarizations h₊(t) and h×(t) generated with source parameters consistent with ten LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA events spanning binary black holes, binary neutron stars and neutron-star-black-hole systems. Being a total derivative in the retarded time, the density is not positive definite and the energy it assigns to a region reduces to a flux across its boundary; as a local diagnostic, however, its morphology correlates with the nature of the source, contrasting the slow, growing oscillation of neutron-star systems with the compact profile that marks a black-hole merger. We argue that this quantity, built directly from the strain, may offer a template-independent diagnostic of gravitational-wave events.
